DATA ART · OUR WORLD IN DATA CO₂ DATASET, 1750–2025

The Human Smokestack

Two artworks about who put the world’s CO₂ into the air: one to see, one to hear.

Melki Chaima · Advanced Data Science · 30/11/2026

THE STORY

Most of humanity’s CO₂ came from a few countries, in a short time. The warming follows the running total.

12%

of all CO₂ ever emitted was released before 1950

68%

of cumulative CO₂ since 1750 comes from just ten countries

0.45 °C

of warming for every 1,000 billion tonnes emitted

[Image: The artwork: a streamgraph of CO₂ emissions by region from 1950 to 2025 pouring out of a factory chimney, each band labelled and ending in its 2025 and cumulative totals]

ARTWORK 1 · DESIGN CHOICES

Smoke from one stack

[Image: Detail of the artwork: the chimney’s smoke runs into the start of the stream, with call-outs about the 1950s and about China written in the cream space]

The metaphor

Every band is smoke from the same chimney: human industry. The bands come straight out of the plume.

The shape

A centred streamgraph shows the total and who emits it in one view, as the bands swap places over time.

ARTWORK 1 · DESIGN CHOICES

Each band ends in its own numbers

[Image: Detail of the artwork’s right edge: region names in a column inside the bands, and beside each band its 2025 emissions and 1950–2025 total in the band’s colour]

No separate legend

The names run in one straight column inside the bands. Each band’s 2025 emissions and 1950–2025 total sit right where it ends, in its colour.

A fair comparison

China, the U.S. and India emit 53% today. The rest of Asia, as a group, emits another 18%: more than the U.S.

The years before 1950

The world had already emitted 226 billion tonnes (12%), mostly the U.S., EU and U.K.

ARTWORK 2 · HEARING

Breath of the Chimney

1850–2025 in 26 seconds · click the video to play, with sound on

ARTWORK 2 · HOW THE SOUND WORKS

Four layers, all computed from the data

Layer | What you hear | The data it carries

Smoke | Filtered noise, like wind or a roaring chimney | World CO₂ each year → loudness

Chord | Three notes: A3, C♯4, E4 | U.S., EU and China CO₂ → loudness of each note

Drone | A low hum that slowly rises | Warming from CO₂ → pitch, one octave per 0.5 °C

Clock | A soft tick | The start of every decade

0.15 seconds per year · synthesised sample by sample in base R · saved as a WAV file. The drone never falls back, because warming follows the running total, not each year’s emissions.

Every band is someone’s smoke. The warming remembers all of it.
